info.bio:
Fastball es una banda Estadounidense de rock, formada en Austin, Texas en 1990. La banda originalmente se llamaba "Magneto U.S.A." pero cambiaron su nombre luego de firmar con Hollywood Records.
En 1998 su album "All the Pain Mone Can Buy" alcanzo las ventas de platino a los seis meses de su lanzamiento y permanecieron en los Billboard´s Top 200 Albums chart durante un año.

scenes.name: Renacimiento pop, Elephant 6 y lounge-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En la primera mitad de los noventa el pop supera ampliamente a la música experimental: la revancha de la melodía tras un cuarto de siglo de sonidos progresivos. La vía más rentable sigue el pop barroco de los últimos Beach Boys, Van Dyke Parks, Big Star y XTC: Jellyfish (Bellybutton), Imperial Teen, Velvet Crush, Material Issue, Eggs, Fountains Of Wayne, Ben Folds Five, Chainsaw Kittens, Barenaked Ladies. El colectivo «Elephant 6» de Georgia y Luisiana es la escuela pop más influyente de la década: Apples In Stereo, Olivia Tremor Control, Neutral Milk Hotel (In The Aeroplane Over The Sea), Elf Power, Of Montreal; y sus herederos Ladybug Transistor y Photon Band. El folk-pop a lo Tom Petty y R.E.M.; el «lounge-pop» (Combustible Edison, Zumpano, Ivy, Cardigans, Squirrel Nut Zippers); el teen-pop (Hanson, Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys).

podcast.title: Discovery of Neglect at Howard Home
podcast.body: On July 3rd, a welfare check at the Howard's home revealed clear signs of cognitive decline, including their hearing aids being left behind and their cat, Happy, found abandoned. This discovery prompted a sick bulletin, a reward offer for their safe return, and extensive media coverage, though it ultimately led to no immediate success in finding the couple. "Given the state of the place, there were obvious signs that the couple were suffering from cognitive decline."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multiple Police Stops in Arkansas
podcast.body: After going missing from Texas, Leila and Ray Howard were pulled over twice by different cops in rural Arkansas on July 2nd. The first stop was for Leila driving with her headlights off, where the trooper noted they were polite but heading in the wrong direction, and Leila seemed to remember their home address. Half an hour later, they were stopped again for driving with high beams on. In both instances, they were let go with a warning, as neither officer realized they were dealing with missing persons. "Neither cop had any idea that they were dealing with a couple of missing persons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Disappearance of Leila and Ray Howard
podcast.body: In 1997, 83-year-old Leila Howard, suffering from early-stage Alzheimer's, and 88-year-old Ray Howard, recovering from brain surgery and a stroke, decided to drive 17 miles from Salado, Texas, to Temple for Pioneer Days. Their son offered to drive, but they declined, asserting they knew the way. They left on Sunday, June 29th, and disappeared, later spotted at a Walmart. This tragic journey inspired Fastball's song "The Way." "The previous year, an elderly couple named Leila and Ray Howard of Solado, Texas decided to go for a drive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragic Death in Arkansas Ravine
podcast.body: Two weeks after leaving their Salado, Texas home, on July 12, 1997, Leila and Ray Howard were found dead in their car at the bottom of a ravine near Hot Springs, Arkansas, almost 450 miles from their house. It is believed Leila may have been trying to find a former vacation spot, and with no skid marks, it appears she drove straight over the 25-foot cliff edge. Ray was found in the passenger seat, while Leila's body was discovered about 20 feet away, still holding her purse and car keys, with the duration their bodies lay there unknown. "Leila and Howard were found dead in their car at the bottom of a ravine near Hot Springs, Arkansas, almost 450 miles from their house."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
